dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.subtitle: A quick look at your Homebrew installation.
dashboard.installHint: mead needs Homebrew installed to do anything. If it's not installed yet, run the official installer from a terminal:

installed.title: Installed
installed.confirmUninstallBody: This removes the package from your system.
installed.checkboxRemoveAppData: Also remove app data (preferences, caches, support files)
installed.checkboxRemoveAppDataCasks: Also remove app data for any casks (preferences, caches, support files)

collections.title: Collections
collections.subtitle: Curated bundles for common workflows. Install everything in one go.

taps.title: Taps
taps.subtitle: Third-party repositories Homebrew can install from.
taps.confirmForceRemoveBody: This untaps it even though it still has installed formulae from it. Those formulae stay installed but become untracked.
taps.removeFailedFallback: Untap failed. It may still have installed formulae from it.

adopt.title: Adopt Existing Apps
adopt.subtitle: Apps already in <path>/Applications</path> that match an installable cask, so future updates can run through Homebrew instead of each app's own updater.
adopt.scanningHint: Checking each app against Homebrew's cask index. This can take a little while.
adopt.nothingToAdopt: Nothing to adopt. Everything matched is already Homebrew-managed (or nothing matched a known cask).

appstore.title: App Store
appstore.subtitle: Mac App Store apps, managed alongside Homebrew via the <cli>mas</cli> CLI.
appstore.installMasDescription: App Store integration needs <link>mas</link>, which is itself a Homebrew formula. Install it and this page will pick up your Mac App Store apps.
appstore.noApps: No Mac App Store apps found.

security.title: Security
security.subtitle: Vulnerability scanning and duplicate-install detection for what you have installed.
security.vulnsDescription: Checks installed formulae against <link>OSV.dev</link>'s public advisory database. Best-effort: casks aren't covered, and a clean scan doesn't guarantee there's nothing wrong, just nothing known.
security.duplicatesDescription: Flags names installed as both a formula and a cask, usually the same tool pulled in twice.
security.missingDescription: Checks installed formulae for a dependency that's supposed to be installed but isn't -- usually the sign of an interrupted install or a manually removed dependency.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.subtitle: Diagnose problems and reclaim disk space.
maintenance.doctorDescription: Checks your system for potential problems that could interfere with Homebrew.
maintenance.doctorAllGood: Your system is ready to brew.
maintenance.clearCacheDescription: Homebrew's normal cleanup keeps recent downloads around (in case you reinstall), so the cache can still show files right after cleaning up. This removes everything in the cache, regardless of age.
maintenance.largestDescription: Largest installed packages. See what's taking up the most disk space.
maintenance.cleanupDescription: Removes old versions of installed formulae and casks, and clears the download cache.
maintenance.autoremoveDescription: Removes formulae that were installed only as a dependency and are no longer needed by anything.
maintenance.exportDescription: Export everything you have installed to a Brewfile, a portable snapshot you can check into a dotfiles repo or use to set up a new machine.
maintenance.importDescription: Install everything listed in an existing Brewfile. Useful for restoring a snapshot on a new machine.
maintenance.checkDescription: Check whether a Brewfile is satisfied, see everything it declares, or preview removing anything installed that isn't in it.
maintenance.cleanupNothingToRemove: Nothing to remove. Everything installed is in the Brewfile.
maintenance.notInBrewfile: Not in the Brewfile, would be removed:
maintenance.confirmRemoveBody:
Not listed in the selected Brewfile:
{{names}}
maintenance.checkboxSnapshot: Create a local safety snapshot first (Time Machine)
maintenance.leftoversDescription: Scans well-known locations (Application Support, Caches, Preferences, Logs, and Saved Application State) for files left behind by apps that aren't currently installed via Homebrew -- either uninstalled outside brew, or never brew-managed at all. This is a best-effort guess, not a guarantee: review carefully before removing anything.
maintenance.confirmDeleteLeftoversBody:
This permanently deletes the selected files and folders. This can't be undone:
{{names}}

history.title: History
history.subtitle: Everything mead has done to your Homebrew installation.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Preferences for mead and for Homebrew itself.
settings.privacyDescription: mead never sends its own commands' analytics to Homebrew (suppressed automatically), but this controls Homebrew's own global analytics preference, the one that also applies if you use `brew` directly in a terminal.
settings.casksDescription: Where cask apps get installed. Leave blank for Homebrew's default (<path>/Applications</path>).
settings.languageDescription: mead's interface language. Detected automatically from your Mac's system language when a translation is available.
settings.languageAutoHint: More languages will show up here as translations are added.
settings.appearanceDescription: Light/dark follows your system setting automatically. Text size:
settings.dataDescription: Favorites, tags, notes, snoozes, and history are stored locally at <path>~/Library/Application Support/mead/store.json</path>. Export a backup, or import one to restore it, useful if the local file is ever lost, or when setting up mead on a new Mac.
settings.confirmClearAllBody: Removes favorites, tags, notes, snoozes, and activity history. This only affects data mead keeps for itself. Nothing installed by Homebrew is touched.
settings.confirmImportBody: Replaces favorites, tags, notes, snoozes, and activity history with the contents of the selected file. Your Settings (like the cask install directory) are left untouched.
